name: gemini_lite_test_v2
description: Test run: all agents use gemini-flash-lite-latest. 3 members (no DevOps).
objective: Build a simple Flask calculator 2.0 web application with add, subtract, multiply, divide operations and an HTML frontend. The app must use Flask with render_template for the UI. Test the app thoroughly. Create a Dockerfile (python:3.11-slim base), run.sh, and README.md as part of the Developer deliverables. Deploy it.

members.responsibilities:
Create a Flask calculator web app. Produce these files in /workspace:
- app.py: Flask app with routes /add, /subtract, /multiply, /divide (accepting query params a and b, returning JSON {"result": value}), plus a root route / serving an HTML calculator UI via render_template.
- templates/index.html: Clean HTML/CSS calculator form that posts to the operation routes and displays results.
- requirements.txt: containing flask.
- Dockerfile: using python:3.11-slim as base, copy app files, pip install -r requirements.txt, expose 5000, CMD ["python3", "app.py"].
- run.sh: startup script.
- README.md: build and run instructions.
Execute the app briefly with `python3 app.py &` then curl each endpoint to verify it works. Kill the server when done.

Test the Flask calculator app created by the Developer.
1. First check /workspace for REVIEW_BRIEF.md and CEREMONY_PLAN.md to understand what was built.
2. Read the actual app.py to understand the routes and expected behavior.
3. Install flask from requirements.txt if needed.
4. Write test_app.py that imports the Flask app from app.py, creates a test client using app.test_client(), and tests all four operations with known inputs.
5. Run the tests with python3 test_app.py.
6. CRITICAL: You MUST write a file called REVIEW_VERDICT.md in /workspace. The FIRST LINE of this file must be exactly PASS or FAIL (nothing else on that line). If tests passed write PASS on line 1, then details below. If tests failed write FAIL on line 1, then what broke below.
Example:
PASS
All 4 operations tested successfully with correct results.

You are the senior reviewer. Your job is to perform a final quality review of the entire project in /workspace before approving deployment.

1. Read ALL files: app.py, templates/index.html, requirements.txt, test_app.py, Dockerfile, run.sh, README.md.
2. Check app.py: correct Flask routes, proper error handling (e.g. division by zero), JSON responses.
3. Check Dockerfile: uses python:3.11-slim base, copies all needed files, installs requirements, exposes 5000.
4. Check test_app.py: covers all 4 operations with correct assertions.
5. CRITICAL: You MUST write a file called FINAL_REVIEW.md in /workspace.
   - The FIRST LINE must be exactly APPROVED or REJECTED (nothing else on that line).
   - Below that, write a summary of what you found and any issues.
6. If APPROVED, also emit EXACTLY this line on its own:
DEPLOYMENT_REQUEST:flask-calculator:5000:python3 app.py
Do NOT wrap it in markdown, do NOT add asterisks or backticks. Just print that exact line on its own.
7. If REJECTED, do NOT emit the deployment request. Explain what needs fixing so the Developer can rework it.

ceremonies.name: Development Review
ceremonies.description: Collect the Developer output and write REVIEW_BRIEF.md so the Tester can see exactly what was built.

ceremonies.name: Test Quality Gate
ceremonies.description: Read the Tester verdict from REVIEW_VERDICT.md. If FAIL, send feedback back to the Developer for rework. If PASS, proceed to Reviewer.

ceremonies.name: Pre-Review Aggregation
ceremonies.description: Aggregate all outputs (Developer code + Tester results) into FINAL_SUMMARY.md before the Reviewer runs.

ceremonies.name: Final Review Gate
ceremonies.description: Read the Reviewer verdict from FINAL_REVIEW.md. If REJECTED, send feedback back to the Developer for rework. If APPROVED, proceed to deployment.
